lessons.title: Get ready! What you will learn

pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 🔤 **Strand 2 — Algebra**
Using letters and symbols to describe patterns, relationships and unknown quantities.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B7.2.2)
- B7.2.2.1 — Simplify algebraic expressions involving the four basic operations and substitute values to evaluate algebraic expressions.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- translate statements and real-life situations into algebraic expressions
- add and subtract like terms
- multiply and divide algebraic terms
- substitute values to evaluate expressions
- use the properties of the four operations to simplify expressions

pages.title: Key words and map
pages.body:
> ✨ **Key words**
- variable
- term
- coefficient
- constant
- like terms
- unlike terms
- expression
- simplify
- substitute
- evaluate

> 🗺️ **Sections in this chapter**
- 6.1 Forming algebraic expressions
- 6.2 Adding and subtracting algebraic expressions
- 6.3 Multiplying and dividing algebraic terms
- 6.4 Substituting values into expressions
- 6.5 Using properties of operations to simplify expressions

pages.title: Forming algebraic expressions
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Create simple algebraic expressions using simple logic to translate a set of instructions into an algebraic expression.
Curriculum indicator B7.2.2.1.1
> 🔑 **Key idea: Variable and expression** — A **variable** is a letter that stands for an unknown number (e.g. x, y, n). An **algebraic expression** combines numbers, variables and operation signs, e.g. 5x + 2. In 5x + 2, the **terms** are 5x and 2; 5 is the **coefficient** of x and 2 is a **constant**.
## ✏️ Example 6.1
If x represents an unknown number, write an expression for each statement.
| **Statement** | **Expression** |
|---|---|
| 10 more than a number | x + 10 |
| 5 less than a number | x − 5 |
| 3 times a number | 3x |
| half of a number | [[1/2]]x or [[x/2]] |
| 2 more than 5 times a number | 5x + 2 |
| 8 times a number is subtracted from 5 and the result is multiplied by 2 | 2(5 − 8x) |
**Solution**
Read each statement slowly and decide which operation is done first. In the last statement the subtraction (5 − 8x) is done first, so it is placed in brackets before multiplying by 2.

pages.title: Example 6.2
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 6.2
Write an expression for each situation.
a) Afrako is 3 years older than Maako. If Maako is x years old, what is Afrako's age?
b) Agbolosu and Tetteh were given GH₵400 to share. Tetteh had GH₵35 more than Agbolosu. If Agbolosu's share is GH₵x, write an expression for Tetteh's share.
c) A woman buys a basket of oranges for x cedis and sells it for y cedis. Find her profit.
d) Find the area of a rectangle which is t metres long and q metres wide.
e) Find the perimeter of a rectangle which is x metres long and y metres wide.
**Solution**
a) **(x + 3) years** b) **GH₵(x + 35)** c) Profit = selling price − cost price = **GH₵(y − x)**
d) Area = length × width = **tq m²** e) Perimeter = x + y + x + y = **2(x + y) m** or (2x + 2y) m
> ⚠️ **Watch out!** Write 3 × x as **3x** (number first, no × sign) and x × y as **xy**. Write 1x simply as **x**.

pages.title: Adding and subtracting algebraic expressions
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Perform addition and subtraction of algebraic expressions with rational coefficients.
Curriculum indicator B7.2.2.1.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: Like and unlike terms** — **Like terms** have exactly the same variables raised to the same powers (e.g. 3x and 7x; 2ab and −5ab). **Unlike terms** do not (e.g. 3x and 3y; x and x²). Only like terms can be added or subtracted — we add or subtract their coefficients.
## ✏️ Example 6.3
Simplify: a) x + x b) y + y + y + y c) s + s + s + t + t + k + k + k
**Solution**
a) **2x** b) **4y** c) **3s + 2t + 3k** (s, t and k are unlike terms, so they cannot be combined)
## ✏️ Example 6.4
Simplify: a) 4x + 3x + x b) 5x + 4x + 2x + 3x c) 3abc + 4abc + 2abc
**Solution**
a) (4 + 3 + 1)x = **8x** b) (5 + 4 + 2 + 3)x = **14x** c) (3 + 4 + 2)abc = **9abc**
## ✏️ Example 6.5
Write an expression for the perimeter of each shape.
[[fig:m7-f25]]
Figure 6.1: Find the perimeter of each shape
**Solution**
a) Rectangle: 2a + b + 2a + b = **4a + 2b**
b) Isosceles triangle: x + x + y = **2x + y**
c) L-shape: going round the boundary: 3p + q + 2p + q + p + 2q = **6p + 4q**
## ✏️ Example 6.6
Simplify: a) 5x − 2x b) 3x − 4x − 2x c) 7x − 4x − x
**Solution**
a) **3x** b) (3 − 4 − 2)x = **−3x** c) (7 − 4 − 1)x = **2x**
## ✏️ Example 6.7
Simplify by collecting like terms:
a) 5x + 4 − 9y + 3x + 2y − 7 b) 2p − 3q + 3p + 5q c) 4x + 7 − 2x − 4 d) 7xy + 5x − 4x + 2xy − 3
**Solution**
a) (5x + 3x) + (−9y + 2y) + (4 − 7) = **8x − 7y − 3**
b) (2p + 3p) + (−3q + 5q) = **5p + 2q**
c) (4x − 2x) + (7 − 4) = **2x + 3**
d) (7xy + 2xy) + (5x − 4x) − 3 = **9xy + x − 3**

pages.title: Keep going
pages.body: > 🎯 **BECE tip** Each term carries the sign in front of it. Underline like terms with the same colour (or shape) before collecting them so that no term is forgotten.

pages.title: Multiplying and dividing algebraic terms
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Perform multiplication and division of algebraic expressions with rational coefficients.
Curriculum indicator B7.2.2.1.3
> 🔑 **Key idea: Multiplying terms** — Multiply the coefficients (taking care with signs), then multiply the variables. Equal letters combine into powers: x × x = x², and x^{2} × x^{3} = x × x × x × x × x = x^{5}.
## ✏️ Example 6.8
Simplify: a) 4p × 8p² b) 5xy² × 4x⁴y³ c) −2a × 4c × 5b d) −3xy × 5y
**Solution**
a) 4 × 8 × p × p² = **32p³**
b) 5 × 4 × (x × x⁴) × (y² × y³) = **20x⁵y⁵**
c) −2 × 4 × 5 × a × b × c = **−40abc**
d) −3 × 5 × x × y × y = **−15xy²**
## ✏️ Example 6.9
Write an expression for the area of each shape.
[[fig:m7-f26]]
Figure 6.2: Find the area of each shape
**Solution**
a) Rectangle: 3x × 2y = **6xy** b) Square: 4a × 4a = **16a²** c) Triangle: [[1/2]] × 6m × 5n = **15mn**
> 🔑 **Key idea: Dividing terms** — Write the division as a fraction, then cancel common factors of the numbers and of each variable: [[x^{5}/x^{2}]] = [[x×x×x×x×x/x×x]] = x³.
## ✏️ Example 6.10
Simplify: a) [[12x^{3}y^{2}/16xy^{4}]] b) [[−30a^{2}bc/6abc]] c) [[18x^{5}y^{2}/24x^{7}y^{2}]]
**Solution**
a) [[12/16]] × [[x^{3}/x]] × [[y^{2}/y^{4}]] = [[3/4]] × x^{2} × [[1/y^{2}]] = [[3x^{2}/4y^{2}]]
b) [[−30/6]] × [[a^{2}/a]] × [[b/b]] × [[c/c]] = **−5a**
c) [[18/24]] × [[x^{5}/x^{7}]] × [[y^{2}/y^{2}]] = [[3/4x^{2}]]

pages.title: Substituting values into expressions
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Substitute values to evaluate algebraic expressions.
Curriculum indicator B7.2.2.1.4
To **evaluate** an expression, replace each variable by its given value (use brackets for negative numbers), then work out the result using the correct order of operations. It is usually easier to **simplify first**.
## ✏️ Example 6.11
If x = 2, y = 4, p = 3 and z = −1, simplify and evaluate:
a) 3xy × 5y b) 7xy + 5x − 4x + 2xy − 3 c) 4p × 8z² d) 5x + 4 − 9y + 3x + 2y − 7
**Solution**
a) 3xy × 5y = 15xy² = 15 × 2 × 4² = 15 × 2 × 16 = **480**
b) = 9xy + x − 3 = 9(2)(4) + 2 − 3 = 72 + 2 − 3 = **71**
c) 4p × 8z² = 32pz² = 32 × 3 × (−1)² = 32 × 3 × 1 = **96**
d) = 8x − 7y − 3 = 8(2) − 7(4) − 3 = 16 − 28 − 3 = **−15**
## ✏️ Example 6.12
If x = 2, y = 4, a = 3, b = 2, z = 1 and c = −1, simplify and evaluate:
a) [[12x^{3}y^{2}/16xy^{4}]] b) [[−30a^{2}bc/6abc]] c) [[18x^{5}y^{2}/24x^{3}y^{2}]] d) [[8xyz/16xy]]
**Solution**
a) = [[3x^{2}/4y^{2}]] = [[3×4/4×16]] = [[12/64]] = [[3/16]]
b) = −5a = −5 × 3 = **−15**
c) = [[3x^{2}/4]] = [[3×4/4]] = **3**
d) = [[z/2]] = [[1/2]]
## ✏️ Example 6.13
If a = 8, b = 3, l = 5 and h = 6, find the perimeter and area of each shape.
[[fig:m7-f27]]
Figure 6.3: Shapes with sides given by letters
**Solution**
a) Rectangle a by h: perimeter = 2(a + h) = 2(8 + 6) = **28 units**; area = ah = 8 × 6 = **48 square units**.
b) Isosceles triangle with equal sides l, base a and height b: perimeter = 2l + a = 10 + 8 = **18 units**; area = [[1/2]]ab = [[1/2]] × 8 × 3 = **12 square units**.

pages.title: Keep going
pages.body: > ⚠️ **Watch out!** When a negative number is squared, the answer is positive: (−1)² = (−1) × (−1) = 1. But −1² means −(1²) = −1. Always put brackets around negative values when substituting.

pages.title: Using properties of operations to simplify expressions
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use properties of the four operations to simplify algebraic expressions with rational coefficients.
Curriculum indicator B7.2.2.1.5
The **commutative** (a + b = b + a; ab = ba), **associative** and **distributive** (a(b + c) = ab + ac) properties, together with the order of operations, let us simplify longer expressions.
## ✏️ Example 6.14
Simplify: a) 3xy × 2 + 6x²y³ ÷ 2xy² b) [[7x + 4x − 2x/7x^{2} + 2x^{2}]] c) 3x²y + 2xy² − 4x²y − 6xy²
**Solution**
a) Do × and ÷ before +: 3xy × 2 = 6xy; 6x²y³ ÷ 2xy² = 3xy. So the expression = 6xy + 3xy = **9xy**.
b) Numerator = 9x; denominator = 9x². [[9x/9x^{2}]] = [[1/x]]
c) Collect like terms: (3x²y − 4x²y) + (2xy² − 6xy²) = **−x²y − 4xy²**
## ✏️ Example 6.15
Simplify: a) (15p³q² × 12x⁵y³) ÷ (36pq × 45xy) b) [[7a − 7a^{3} + 14a^{4}/7a]] c) [[6x^{4} − 9x^{3}/3x^{2}]]
**Solution**
a) Numerator: 15 × 12 p³q²x⁵y³ = 180p³q²x⁵y³. Denominator: 36 × 45 pqxy = 1,620pqxy.
[[180/1620]] × p^{2}qx^{4}y^{2} = [[p^{2}qx^{4}y^{2}/9]]
b) Divide each term by 7a: [[7a/7a]] − [[7a^{3}/7a]] + [[14a^{4}/7a]] = **1 − a² + 2a³**
c) [[6x^{4}/3x^{2}]] − [[9x^{3}/3x^{2}]] = **2x² − 3x**

pages.title: Chapter 6 summary
pages.body:
- An expression is built from terms; a term has a coefficient and variables.
- Only like terms can be added or subtracted.
- To multiply terms, multiply coefficients and combine powers of the same letter; to divide, cancel common factors.
- To evaluate, substitute values (with brackets for negatives) and follow the order of operations.
